rules.response: When Python shows an error, read the traceback from the bottom up: the last line tells you the error type and message; above it shows the line number where it happened. Common beginner errors: SyntaxError, NameError, TypeError, IndexError, ZeroDivisionError, KeyError.
A ZeroDivisionError occurs when you divide a number by zero (10 / 0). Fix it by checking the divisor before dividing: if b != 0: result = a / b else: print('Cannot divide by zero').

Use try/except to handle errors without crashing: try: risky_code() except ErrorType: handle_it(). The 'except' block only runs if the specified error occurs in the 'try' block. Use 'except Exception as e: print(e)' to catch and display any error.

input() pauses the program and waits for the user to type something. It always returns a string: user_name = input('Enter your name: '). To get a number, convert it: age = int(input('Enter your age: ')). Without conversion, arithmetic will cause a TypeError.

print() displays values to the screen. You can pass multiple values separated by commas: print('Hello', name). For formatted output, use f-strings: print(f'Hello, {name}! You are {age} years old.') — variables go inside curly braces {}.
I can only help with beginner Python topics: variables, data types, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, lists, dictionaries, error types, and basic I/O. Try asking about one of those topics!
